Target's Advil value bundle is 320 plain ibuprofen 200 mg tablets, and Target's own up&up ibuprofen 200 mg, an FDA-approved generic of Advil, costs about a sixth as much per tablet.

The kit: $26.11 plus $5.99 delivery. You keep $7.53 today.
Where the kit differs
Advil tablets have a sugar coating; up&up tablets are film coated and the 200-count is caplet shaped. Inactive ingredients differ. The saving is per tablet: the up&up packs hold 1,200 tablets for $18.58, so you pay less in total than the bundle but buy far more than 320 tablets. Ibuprofen keeps for years, but check the expiry date before buying the 1000 pack. Advil's 20-count was not sold on its own at Target, so its price comes only from the bundle.
How we checked each item
Target sells the bundle as one listing at $26.11 (Advil 300ct + Advil 20ct coated tablets). Advil's DailyMed label (Haleon) gives 'Ibuprofen 200 mg (NSAID)' per coated tablet and lists the 300-tablet bottle. The up&up ibuprofen tablet label on DailyMed (Target Corporation) gives 'Ibuprofen 200 mg (NSAID)' per film-coated tablet, says 'Compare to active ingredient in Advil' and is approved under ANDA072096, which means the FDA found it bioequivalent to the brand. Target's twin pack (2 x 500) is $14.29 (1.4 cents a tablet) and the up&up 200-count coated caplets are $4.29 and state 'Compare to the active ingredient in Advil Ibuprofen Caplets'. In the Chicago Booth / NBER study 'Do Pharmacists Buy Bayer?' (Bronnenberg, Dube, Gentzkow and Shapiro), pharmacists bought national-brand headache remedies only 9% of the time, against 26% for the average shopper.
